svg.text: The migration agent - one contract, any runtime, any vendor
A facade: one A2A Agent Card fronts swappable backends. "Claude vs Kimi on the same ten migrations" is a config change, not a rewrite.
any A2A caller - coordinator · curl · Make.com · cron
migration.run - the one Agent Card (:4003 · content-factory-migrate.jackzhaojin.com)
{ sourceType, sourceLocation, site, owner, pageSlug, folder?, pattern?, neighborPageUrl?, guidance?, backend?, … }
Surfaces: /a2a (JSON-RPC + SSE) · /hooks/migration/migration.run (flat POST + callback webhook - no A2A needed) · /callbacks/makecom/:taskId
The backend is an implementation detail: payload.backend, else MIGRATION_DEFAULT_BACKEND. Same MigrationResult artifact out of every one.
guidance channel: the site profile's standing principles + the run's free-text guidance are merged into the prompt; unsatisfiable principles land in the report's gaps
MigrationBackend seam - assertConfigured() + run()
dryrun - deterministic simulation, $0
previewUrl = sourceLocation (a perfect pretend migration)
confidence derived from the slug hash - CI + demos run on this
makecom - a low-code cloud scenario does the work
webhook out (10 fields + callbackUrl) → Make.com authors the page
→ callback in, bearer-gated; a parked waiter OR the store completes it
restart-tolerant: a scenario outliving our process still lands
the same pattern as A2A push notifications - evented, not held open
sdk - Claude (Anthropic) as the author
the Claude Agent SDK drives the same prompt, skill, and MCP servers
model per run: Sonnet 5 · Opus 5 · Haiku 4.5 (subscription OAuth)
opencode - Kimi (Moonshot) as the author ★ the vendor-swap proof
a long-lived `opencode serve` + REST; one A2A task = one agentic session
model per run: k3 (default) · kimi-for-coding (a moving alias - resolved live)
da.live MCP
the deployed functions/ server;
CRUD + preview-publish; self-auths
to da.live via its own S2S account
no client credential needed
Playwright MCP
agentic eyes: read the legacy
source, then screenshot + validate
the published preview, refine ≤ N
self-validation, in the loop
da-live-author-playwright - skill-as-a-service
the SAME skill file a human Claude session uses, executed headlessly by another vendor's model
observability: the /event SSE stream surfaces every tool call live - K3 → dalive_save_dalive_content
a real turn runs 9-20 min (undici's 300s fetch timeout is disabled mesh-wide, or it dies at 5:01)
makecom + sdk author the same target
create → preview-publish → validate
da.live / Edge Delivery Services (the target - main--adapt-to-2026-demo--jackzhaojin.aem.page)
/ai-content/** - the hand-built REFERENCE corpus the migrator learns block conventions from (GET the neighbor page, mimic it) - agents never write here
/ai-articles/** and dated demo folders - where agent-authored pages land, preview-only (.aem.page)
Nothing in the mesh can touch .aem.live - the production publish does not exist as a capability. Promote-to-live is a human-gated future skill by design.

The seam is the point. A simulation, a low-code cloud scenario, and a non-Anthropic frontier model all serve the identical migration.run contract - callers cannot tell which ran except by reading the report.
Verified end-to-end: Kimi authored a real da.live page from inside a Cloudflare container and the real eval scored it 91 - one pipeline, two model vendors, zero contract changes.
